rounds.text: Active Clothing Co Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity as its fundamentals are vastly outpacing its current market valuation, evidenced by a staggering 178% compounded profit growth over five years while the 5-year share price growth lagged significantly at 29% [E19, E22, E45]. Operational efficiency is underscored by a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.40x for March 2026, meaning reported profits of Rs 14 Cr are fully backed by actual operating cash flows [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the completion of capital expenditure is signaled by CWIP dropping to zero, indicating that new capacity is ready to come online [E38], while the textiles sector enjoys a supportive macro tailwind score of +0.53 [E57, E59]. Conceded: the company carries a high leverage risk with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.66x and borrowings of Rs 164 Cr, alongside a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E36, E37].

Active Clothing Co Ltd carries significant financial risk due to its heavy debt burden, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.66x as of September 2026 and borrowings expanding to Rs 164 Cr from Rs 130 Cr a year prior [E36, E37]. This aggressive leverage coincides with negative free cash flow of Rs -3 Cr in March 2026 and a complete absence of dividend payouts, yielding 0.00% [E4, E35]. Furthermore, profitability metrics reveal structural headwinds: operating margins have compressed from 10% to 8% over three years and dropped to 6% in the September 2026 quarter, while the yearly and quarterly margin trends are officially flagged as inconsistent [E29, E30, E31, E32]. Longer-term return metrics further weaken the valuation case, evidenced by a low median return on equity of 6% over 10 years and 7% over 5 years, accompanied by explicit flags regarding low 3-year ROE and potential interest cost capitalization [E25, E26, E50, E51]. Price performance reflects these underlying fundamental strains, with compounded share price growth contracting by -8% over the past year and the stock languishing at just 14% of its 52-week range [E5, E24]. Conceded: the company displays robust medium-term sales and profit compounding alongside strong recent top-line growth [E15, E16, E19, E20, E53], and its EV/EBITDA of 9.5x sits close to the sector benchmark of 9x [E11].

Conceded: debt-to-equity is 1.66x and free cash flow was negative at Rs -3 Cr [E35, E36]. However, this borrowing coincides with a 100% reduction in Capital Work in Progress down to Rs 0 Cr, proving that capex is largely completed and new capacity is actively coming online to drive future output [E38]. Operating cash flow remains robust at Rs 14 Cr with a healthy cash conversion of 1.40x, fully backing reported profits with actual cash [E33, E34]. While the bear highlights compressed margins and an -8% 1-year share price return [E24, E29, E30], fundamentals have drastically outpaced sentiment: 5-year profit growth stands at an extraordinary 178% against a share price growth of only 29%, showing that fundamental outperformance has completely disconnected from the stagnant price [E22, E45]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 289 per share against a market price of Rs 94.8, leaving a massive margin of safety of 67.2% [E42, E43], and the reverse DCF indicates the current price merely prices in a modest 2.6% growth rate compared to the 18.0% base case [E44].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 14 Cr with a cash conversion of 1.40x in Mar 2026 [E33, E34]. However, the bull's claim that completed capex validates rising debt [E36, E37, E38] ignores that free cash flow remains negative at Rs -3 Cr [E35], meaning operations are still burning cash despite finished work-in-progress. Furthermore, pointing to a 178% five-year profit growth [E19] masks a weak historical baseline, as evidenced by a 10-year median return on equity of just 6% and a 5-year median ROE of 7% [E25, E26], alongside a low 3-year average ROE of 10.4% [E50]. While the DCF model suggests a wide margin of safety [E42, E43], the company's operating margins have deteriorated by 2 percentage points both over the trailing twelve months and in the most recent quarter [E29, E30], accompanied by an inconsistent margin trend [E31, E32]. Finally, the negative 1-year share price return of -8% [E24] and zero dividend yield [E4, E49] confirm that fundamental growth has failed to reward shareholders or generate distributable cash.
